correctness.rationale: On the orthonormal Gaussian Fock monomials the numerator is Σ_{n≥0}|Σ_j c_j b_j^n|² and the denominator is Σ_j |c_j|²/(1−|b_j|²). Thus the optimum is the least eigenvalue of G_{ij}=√[(1−|b_i|²)(1−|b_j|²)]/(1−conj(b_i)b_j); the first N coordinates make it positive definite. Write σ_j=∏_{k≠j}(b_j−b_k)/(1−conj(b_k)b_j), and E=diag(1/σ_j). Independently, the exact normalized Cauchy inverse is G⁻¹=E Gᵀ E*. A conjugation check: normalized Hardy functions u_j=√(1−|b_j|²)k_{b_j} have Gram Gᵀ in the conjugate-first convention; their biorthogonal functions are σ_j⁻¹ B(z) conj(z) conj(u_j(z)) on the circle, with B the finite Blaschke product of all slopes. These are analytic since B(z)/(z−b_j) is analytic, and their normalized evaluations give the identity. The boundary conjugation is anti-isometric; transposing the dual Gram gives the stated G⁻¹. At the collision, ε^(N−1)/σ_j→(1−|a|²)^(N−1)w_j and Gᵀ→11ᵀ. This yields the claimed positive rank-one inverse limit, eigenvalue coefficient and line. Alternatively, the O(ε^(N−1)) operator norm on unit minimizing coefficients forces Σ_j c_j ζ_j^m=O(ε^(N−1−m)) for m≤N−2 by the binomial identity on (b_j−a)^m. The limiting nullspace is the barycentric line by the Vandermonde interpolation identity. For regular slopes discrete Fourier modes retain the coordinates n in a single residue class, yielding eigenvalues N(1−ε²)ε^(2s)/(1−ε^(2N)), s=0,…,N−1. The smallest is s=N−1. The actual fixed interior-center hypotheses and separate center-zero identity are valid. The supplied script was inspected, not run.
residual_risks: The coefficient is a fixed-center, fixed-N asymptotic for distinct directions; no uniform joint scaling to the unit circle or to N→∞, or conclusion for other Schatten exponents, is assessed.

originality.rationale: This is mechanically covered by exact classical Cauchy inversion on the very same matrix, not just analogous to earlier cluster conditioning. Fock simultaneous diagonalization gives a normalized multiplicative Cauchy matrix, and Cauchy double alternants on all minors plus the adjugate give its full inverse, equivalently G⁻¹=E Gᵀ E* above. To see coverage even without phases, det G=∏_{i<j}|(b_i−b_j)/(1−conj(b_i)b_j)|². Thus tr G⁻¹=Σ_j |σ_j|⁻² by the principal minors. The order-two principal minors of G⁻¹ are complementary determinants divided by det G, so each is O(ε^(−4N+6)), while (tr G⁻¹)² has order ε^(−4N+4). One inverse eigenvalue therefore carries the full leading trace; the exact inverse also gives its line directly, or that line follows from the vanishing Vandermonde moments. The regular-polygon identity is the elementary geometric series in each discrete Fourier residue class. There is no additional calculation beyond these standard exact implications. This fail is not a claim that a fixed-symbol Fock paper prints the collision limit, nor that the overlapping same-day catalogue record takes priority.
residual_risks: No independently recovered full comparison with the distinct same-day b96c3b6b80d6 result, the old two-operator paper, or the complete initiating Fock paper. No ordering or literal duplication is concluded; the exact classical implication already establishes coverage.
